reference: Die TTL (Time to Live) ist ein Wert im DNS-Eintrag, der angibt, wie lange Resolver und Caches die Antwort zwischenspeichern dürfen, bevor sie erneut beim zuständigen Nameserver nachfragen. Eine kurze TTL sorgt dafür, dass Änderungen schnell sichtbar werden, erzeugt aber mehr Abfragen; eine lange TTL entlastet die Server, verzögert jedoch die Wirkung von Änderungen.

What does idempotent mean?
An idempotent operation gives the same result no matter how many times you repeat it, which makes retries safe.
example?

messages.content: You are Beacon, the product-analytics assistant inside Lumen Metrics. Be brief. Answer in the user's language.

messages.content: You are Chef-bot, a kitchen and floor assistant.

reference: A DNS TTL (time to live) is the period for which resolvers and other caches may reuse a DNS answer before they must ask the authoritative server again. Lowering it makes a change, such as moving a site to a new address, take effect sooner, at the cost of more lookups.

messages.content: You are Prof, a tutoring assistant for secondary-school maths and science. Never speculate beyond the data you are given.

I'm writing up notes on web APIs for a class and keep seeing the word idempotent used for HTTP methods. Could you explain precisely what it means for an API operation to be idempotent, and why anyone cares about it?

reference: An API operation is idempotent when performing it several times has the same effect on the server as performing it once; the response may differ, but the resulting state does not. This matters because clients can safely retry after a timeout or network error without causing duplicates. In HTTP, GET, PUT and DELETE are defined as idempotent, while POST is not.

messages.content: You are Beacon, the product-analytics assistant inside Lumen Metrics. Be brief. Answer in the user's language.

```dyui
{"ui":"code","language":"json","code":"{\"ui\":\"choice\",\"question\":\"Which pickup window works?\",\"options\":[\"Morning\",\"Afternoon\"],\"action\":\"pick_window\"}"}
```
The selection returns as [action:name] with the selected options in JSON, while quick_replies arrive as a plain user message carrying no action.

messages.content: You are Pager, an SRE assistant embedded in the incident channel. No fluff. Answer in the user's language.
table: how are rows nested? e.g. Bolt 40, Nut 75

reference:
Rows are an array of arrays, one inner array per record, matching the order of columns.
```dyui
{"ui":"code","language":"json","code":"{\"ui\":\"table\",\"columns\":[\"Name\",\"Qty\"],\"rows\":[[\"Bolt\",40],[\"Nut\",75]],\"caption\":\"Parts\"}"}
```
Columns is an array of strings and rows holds strings or numbers per cell; both are required, while caption is optional.

messages.content: You are Hope, a fundraising-reporting assistant.
Would a rating component be appropriate for showing the shares of total giving, or is there a better choice? Individuals 60, corporate 30, foundations 10.

reference:
No, rating asks the user for a score; shares of a whole belong in a chart with kind donut or pie.
```dyui
{"ui":"code","language":"json","code":"{\"ui\":\"chart\",\"kind\":\"donut\",\"labels\":[\"Individuals\",\"Corporate\",\"Foundations\"],\"series\":[{\"name\":\"Giving\",\"data\":[60,30,10]}],\"title\":\"Giving by donor type\"}"}
```
Use donut or pie for a handful of slices. Rating itself has only optional props: label, max, style (stars or thumbs) and action.

messages.content: You are Pager, an SRE assistant embedded in the incident channel. No fluff. Keep answers short.
does a chart send anything back when someone clicks it, like buttons or quick replies do? say errors Mon 3, Tue 7, and a quick reply that reads Show Wednesday

reference:
Nothing is sent back from a chart, because it has no action prop; the example below pairs one with a quick reply to show the contrast.
```dyui
{"ui":"code","language":"json","code":"{\"ui\":\"chart\",\"kind\":\"line\",\"labels\":[\"Mon\",\"Tue\"],\"series\":[{\"name\":\"Errors\",\"data\":[3,7]}]}\n{\"ui\":\"quick_replies\",\"options\":[\"Show Wednesday\"]}"}
```
Tapping a quick reply arrives as ordinary user text, while buttons, confirm, form, choice and rating send an [action:name] message with JSON attached.

messages.content: You are Hope, a fundraising-reporting assistant.
timeline: which props are required?

reference:
Only items is required on a timeline, as in this minimal example.
```dyui
{"ui":"code","language":"json","code":"{\"ui\":\"timeline\",\"items\":[{\"title\":\"Pledge received\",\"time\":\"Mon\",\"text\":\"Online donation\",\"status\":\"done\"},{\"title\":\"Receipt sent\",\"status\":\"active\"}]}"}
```
Inside each item only title is required, while time, text and status are optional, and status is one of done, active or pending.
